News.title: Starmer hits the pub after handing over keys to Andy Burnham as a relieved Rachel Reeves laughs with vaping aides
News.content:
BITTER, KEIR? Starmer hits the pub after handing over keys to Andy Burnham as a relieved Rachel Reeves laughs with vaping aides

SIR Keir Starmer headed straight for a pint of bitter at his local pub after stepping down as Prime Minister.

He made a beeline for a pub in Kentish Town with loyalists including Rachel Reeves hours after handing over the keys to No10 to Andy Burnham.



In exclusive pics obtained by The Sun, Starmer is spotted clutching a pint while his ex-Chancellor Rachel Reeves grins delightedly between gulps of wine.

Earlier, Sir Keir had delivered a short goodbye speech outside Downing Street and travelled to Buckingham Palace to formally resign to King Charles, ending his two tumultuous years in office.



He said serving as Prime Minister had been “the privilege of my life” and insisted he left office “with good grace and with a smile”.

Sir Keir reflected on taking Labour from its crushing 2019 election defeat to a landslide victory in 2024, declaring: “My work is done.”

The former Labour leader insisted Britain was now “stronger and fairer” than when he entered No10, pointing to a stronger economy, falling NHS waiting lists, lower immigration and increased defence spending among his Government’s achievements.

But he also struck a warning note, saying Britain’s enemies would “stop at nothing to divide us” because of the country’s values and unwavering support for Ukraine.



He added: “And so, under this attack, it is vital that we remember the greatness of the Britain all around us.

“That while we debate how to fix our problems, there is something we inherit from our country and our character that can give us confidence that we can change our country for the better, that we can create a Britain where every child can go as far as their talent will take them, and we can unite different people under our common flag if we don’t succumb to that division.”

Turning to his successor, he said: “As I now pass the baton to Andy Burnham, I wish him every success. He has my full support.”

Sir Keir ended by thanking wife Victoria, their children, his staff, Labour activists and civil servants, saying politics would always be “a team sport”.

He concluded: “I thank the British people for the opportunity to serve. I go with good grace. I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved.”



The speech lasted less than five minutes before the former PM left Downing Street for the final time and headed to Buckingham Palace to tender his resignation to the King.

Within the hour, Mr Burnham had been invited to form a Government and returned to No10 as Britain’s new Prime Minister.

Leaving behind the pomp of Westminster, the former PM headed to his local pub, where family, friends and his closest advisers gathered for a private farewell.



Sir Keir swept into No10 with a landslide majority in 2024, promising to restore stability after years of Conservative rule.

But less than two years later, his authority had been battered by the Peter Mandelson’s appointment as US ambassador, Cabinet resignations and internal Labour rows.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The final blow came after Labour’s heavy defeats in the local elections, which triggered intense pressure from MPs for a change at the top.

Sir Keir announced he would step aside last month after Mr Burnham’s stonking victory in the Makerfield by-election, which paved the way for his unopposed win in theLabour leadership.

News.title: Andrew Tate & brother Tristan will remain behind bars as they appear in court fighting extradition to UK after arrest
News.content:
TATES IN COURT Andrew Tate & brother Tristan will remain behind bars as they appear in court fighting extradition to UK after arrest

ANDREW and Tristan Tate were hauled before a US court earlier today as they face extradition to the UK over further rape charges.

The online influencers were arrested by federal authorities in Miami on Saturday after the CPS authorised 38 more rape charges against them.



The new counts relate to the alleged sexual abuse of four additional women in Britain between July 2010 and August 2017.

The brothers were detained as they arrived at a bareknuckle boxing event, before being handcuffed and taken into custody.



They made their first appearance before a federal magistrate at the Wilkie D. Ferguson Jr Courthouse in Miami on Monday afternoon.

US prosecutors are seeking to extradite them to the UK.

A district judge will consider whether they meet the conditions over the coming weeks.



The Tates’ lawyer Joseph McBride confirmed that the brothers will fight the move.

Speaking outside the court after the preliminary hearing, he said: “Today was about enforcing Andrew and Tristan Tate’s rights and objecting to the extradition process. We are of course objecting to extradition because Andrew and Tristan are innocent.”

He claimed his clients are the victims of a “political witch hunt” and are being “attacked for what they say, not what they’ve done”.

The lawyer also branded Britain “a fallen state that prosecutes its citizens for free speech” and suggested US President Donald Trump could intervene in the proceedings, saying “he was elected to fight against this kind of nonsense”.



Self-styled misogynist Andrew, 39, faces 32 further counts, including seven rape charges and 19 involving extreme pornography and indecent images of children.

Tristan, 38, faces six more, including two rape and sex-trafficking charges.

They already faced 21 charges between them relating to three alleged victims, so will now be prosecuted for 59 allegations relating to seven women.



The brothers have previously denied any wrongdoing.

Mr McBride added: “We’ve never seen a scintilla of evidence that indicates that these guys are guilty of anything…You can love them, you can hate them, but nobody should go to jail for free speech, and that is exactly what this is about.

“Make no mistake about it, the United Kingdom was once the greatest empire the world has ever known. It is a fallen nation.

“It is a fallen state that prosecutes its citizens for free speech.”

He added: “That is not what democracies and free societies do. That is what communist China and despotic regimes do.



“And we’re going to fight them at every turn, at every corner, because they are American citizens.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Tates were born in the US before moving to Luton as children.

They are now based in Romania, where they were initially arrested in 2022.

News.title: Woman ‘raped’ in broad daylight at popular park as cops launch urgent probe
News.content:
'RAPE' HORROR Woman ‘raped’ in broad daylight at popular park as cops launch urgent probe

A WOMAN has been taken to hospital after allegedly being raped at a park in broad daylight.

Officers found the injured woman at a Sandwell park in the West Midlands on Monday at around 10.15am.



She was rushed to hospital for assessment having believed to have been raped.

Specially trained officers have been supporting her since being discharged.



West Midlands Police is now calling for any witnesses in Sandwell Valley Country Park from between 8am to 11am to contact it on 101 quoting 20/304639/26.

Detective Inspector Phil Griffiths said: “In the last three weeks officers have been reviewing CCTV footage from around Sandwell Valley Country Park, examining forensic evidence, and speaking to anyone who may have vital information about what happened.



“Neighbourhood officers have been patrolling the area since the incident and specialist officers will be revisiting the park today to speak to anyone who may have information.

“We know the park would have been busy on a Monday morning with people enjoying the sunshine. We need to hear from you if you saw anything that was suspicious.“

News.title: Watch hilarious moment politician pauses mid-interview during live broadcast to shout at his dog
News.content:
THIS is the moment a politician suddenly loses his cool and screams at a dog during a live TV interview.

Footage from the incident shows Australian MP Barnaby Joyce begin his answer before suddenly erupting and shouting “SIT DOWN!”



Joyce was being interviewed on ABC News when the blooper unfolded at around 7:30pm on Monday.

The TV anchor Sarah Ferguson had been pressing him on an important issue about his defection to another party.



She said the leader of his new party was “dragging you further into a place of intolerance and racial discrimination”.

The interviewer added: “You’re defending your leader, but are you really comfortable with where she is taking you?”



The flush-faced politician responded with a meditative “I think…” before suddenly bursting out “SIT DOWN!”

He then retracted his flushed face and told the startled interviewer: “Sorry, it’s a dog”.

He then emitted a short chuckle before beginning his answer again.

One political reporter shared the moment on X and dubbed it the “TV blooper of the year”.



Remarkably, it’s not the first time the MP has raged against a pet dog.

In May 2015, Joyce vowed to kill Johnny Depp’s canines after accusing the Hollywood A-lister of smuggling the Yorkshire terriers into the country on a private jet.

The move was a violation of Australia’s biosecurity and import laws and could have brought a deadly disease into the nation.



Joyce waded in on the drama and said: “If we start letting movie stars—even though they’ve been the sexiest man alive twice—to come into our nation [and break the laws], then why don’t we just break the laws for everybody?

He added: “If he doesn’t take Boo and Pistol back, we do have to euthanize them.”

“The reason you can walk through a park in Brisbane and not have in the back of your mind, ‘What happens if a rabid dog comes out and bites me or bites my kid?’ is because we’ve kept that disease out.”

Depp’s then-partner Amber Heard mocked the MP for his hardline stance.

She quipped on Twitter: “To comfort Mr. Joyce in his hour [of] need, I have sent him a box of New Zealand’s finest kiwi fruit (assuming this passes his biosecurity laws).”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

In 2021, the actress adopted a new dog and named it Barnaby Joyce.

The MP was flattered and suggested that he was still living in Heard’s head “rent free” six years later.

News.title: Bizarre moment Chinese & Filipino sailors in dinghies whack each other with oars & batons as one injured
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment Chinese and Filipino sailors beat each other with oars and long sticks in the hotly disputed waters of the South China Sea.

Footage shows members of the Chinese Coast Guard and Philippine Navy clashing, metres from the rusty LST-542-class tank landing ship BRP Sierra Madre.



The melee happened at the Second Thomas Shoal, where the Philippines maintains a small garrison aboard the vessel.

The Philippine military accused Chinese sailors of repeatedly hitting one of their seamen on the head with a wooden baton and injuring him.



The strike was captured on video by other Filipino sailors, setting off the furious condemnations by officials.

Jay Tarriela, Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) officer, described the incident as a “violent assault.”



“Striking an unarmed sailor on the head with a baton – inside our own exclusive economic zone – in not law enforcement,” he warned.

“it is unlawful aggression, plain and simple.”

Meanwhile, China‘s coast guard hit back claiming that two rubber boats belonging to an “illegally” stationed vessel – meaning the BRP Sierra Madre – had rammed the Chinese patrol boat “in a dangerous manner.”

“During the incident, Philippine personnel maliciously attacked Chinese law enforcement personnel using oars and long sticks,” the Chinese coast guard said in a statement on social media.



Guo Wei, deputy spokesperson of China’s Embassy in Manila, also fired back on X, saying that the Philippines “can’t start a fight and then play then victim.”

He added: “Ignoring repeated warnings from the Chinese side, Philippine personnel continued their provocations, deliberately stirred up trouble, and maliciously attacked Chinese law enforcement officers with paddles, long poles and other objects.”

The Second Thomas Shoal has been the centre of a number of nasty rows in recent years, though this is one of the most dramatic.



Known as Ayungin Shoal in the Philippines and Ren’ai Reef in China, it lies within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone, but Beijing claims it as its own.

In his statement, Tarriela said that “no amount of coercion, violence, or deception can change that.”

Previously, China has demanded that Manila pull away the long-marooned and now rusting navy ship, which serves as a fragile territorial outpost.

The long-simmering dispute, which also involves territorial claims by Brunei, Malaysia, Vietnam and Taiwan, is high in the agenda of annual talks in Manila this week.

Both sides have been negotiating a non-aggression pact that aims to stop a major armed conflict that could draw in the US.



An ally of the Philippines in the region, the US has vowed to help deter the growing Chinese aggression and defend freedom of navigation in the busy waterway.

News.title: How brazen scammers are taking over UK homes to make brothels & drug farms…while owners face ‘no help’ from police
News.content:
FOUR years ago, landlord Craig Shepheard welcomed a new tenant claiming to be a courier into a two bedroom flat he owned in Hertfordshire.

The first few months passed by without issue until, suddenly the rent payments stopped.



Then came complaints from neighbours about cannabis use, and reports of men visiting the flat at night.

“The vast majority of my tenants are absolutely lovely,” Craig told BBC Panorama as part of their investigation into criminals taking over homes, set to air tonight.



“I was using a professional lettings agency, and they got this chap in. He had passed all of his tenancy checks.”

When the tenant told Craig the washing machine was broken, he used the opportunity to investigate what had happened to his flat.

Finding sexual paraphernalia inside, he reported to the police that his flat seemed to be being used as a brothel, but was told they needed more evidence to get a search warrant.

Craig turned detective himself and started filming.

“I opened the door, and there was a double bed there with a blonde naked lady, covered in tattoos, fast asleep on the bed,” he said.

“Through into the second bedroom, there was another double bed, and a man and lady asleep on the bed. And she screamed because there was a strange bloke standing at the doorway, and then the first lady came out with her dressing gown and that’s when we started having a conversation.”



Both women, it turned out, had been paying hundreds each week to rent out the room from someone else.

Hertfordshire Police told Craig that they had been part of an organised prostitution ring, run by a network in Brazil, and that they operated pop-up brothels across England.

The lettings agency that had met the tenant and seen proof of identity had been fooled by a high-quality forgery.



Though Craig was able to track down the tenant and get him to give up the flat, he was down four and a half months’ unpaid rent and faced a £4,500 repair bill to make it suitable to rent again.

In the end, the sex workers vanished, and Hertfordshire Police closed the case due to “lack of evidence”.

Similar stories are playing out across the UK, with criminals able to rack up thousands of pounds worth of profit from these illegal operations while facing little to no threat of retribution.

In South London, Monica was faced with a nightmare after renting out her flat to someone who – on paper – seemed perfect.

The so-called accountant passed reference checks with flying colours and had a British passport.



Six months later, the downstairs neighbours rang her up as water was pouring into their from the flat Monica was letting out above them.

“I found out there was a cannabis farm on my property,” Monica said.

“I was absolutely petrified. I had no idea what had happened to the place.”

Police raided the flat and found more than 60 plants with a street value of an estimated £75,000.



The flood had been caused by an issue with the farm’s complex irrigation system.

Inside, the flat was “horrendous”, Monica added.

“They had blackened out all the windows. The actual cannabis smell was unbelievable.

“There’s mold everywhere, due to the humidity. The floors were completely gone.”



A Vietnamese man was arrested but later released without charge, with police suspecting he was a victim of modern slavery.

Monica told BBC Panorama that she received little support from the Metropolitan Police, who told the program they were still investigating.

Worst of all for Monica is that, six months on from the farm being found in her flat, she still did not have it back as the tenancy agreement was still valid.

Housing law requires landlords to go through a lengthy process of serving a notice and applying for a court date in order to secure an eviction.

However, backlogs and delays mean in many cases the entire process can last between six months to a year.



Monica herself applied for a court date in April and has only just had one confirmed for August.

Again, as with Craig’s flat, the tenant had used a fake passport to pass reference and identify checks.

“The use of false identities is growing almost exponentially,” said Simon Miller, who works for fraud prevention database Cifas.



“Fraud in the UK has become endemic. It’s 45 per cent of all crime, and ID fraud is a really significant part of that.”

In order to find out just how easy it is to obtain fake identity documents these days, BBC Panorama journalist Hazel Martin went onto the internet and found it awash with options.

For just £75, she was able to obtain a completely realistic-looking driver’s licence with her photo, but someone else’s details.

Crucially for the fraud to work, the details on it are based on a real person – someone whose name, address, and data have been stolen and are for sale online.

False ID documents based on legitimate details are much more valuable to criminals, as when those details are passed through verification checks, they will show up as real.



Hazel managed to get in touch with the person whose details were being sold online to create false documentation and warn them.

However, when Hazel tried to report the fraud to the City of London Police, who oversee reporting cybercrime, she was told he could not report it as a crime as she was not the victim.

In addition to brothels and cannabis farms, others have their properties illegally rented out on platforms such as AirBnB.



Neha told BBC Panorama how she had begun renting her flat to a tenant claiming to be a data scientist.

However, neighbours soon alerted her that the tenants had been illegally renting their flat out on AirBnB.

She secured an eviction notice, but just days before they got the flat back, the criminal tenants emptied the flat of all its furniture into the back of a van.

When they were finally able to go back round, they found their flat ransacked and the balcony window smashed.

Looking at the other properties the gang had on AirBnB, Neha saw her stolen furniture being used in the listings.



Despite filing four complaints to the Metropolitan Police over identity fraud, criminal damage, and theft, no one has been arrested in the two and a half months since the ordeal.

“We have done all the hard work of gathering all the evidence. But there have been zero repercussions just yet,” said Neha.

“This makes me believe that this is the perfect crime.”



The Metropolitan Police said that they are still investigating the case.

BBC Panorama tracked down the person whose name had been used on the ID documents to rent Neha’s flat – a woman called Poonan Grover, who lived in north London

She looked nothing like the woman on the ID documents, which, it turned out, was an image of a model available online.

It turned out that her details had been used multiple times, and she had even been threatened by debt collectors over unpaid rent that had nothing to do with her.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In reality, Poonan was one of many around the country who are victims of identity fraud.



To date, none of the fraudsters or criminals in the BBC Panorama documentary had been arrested or tried.

News.title: Josh Kerry, 28, charged after Ann Widdecombe found dead with head wound following ‘targeted attack’ at her home
News.content:
JOSHUA Kerry, 28, has been charged after Ann Widdecombe was found dead in her bungalow with a head wound following a “targeted attack”.

He was arrested in Rotherham, South Yorkshire – nearly 300 miles from the Devon home where the ex-Tory minister, 78, was found a week and a half ago.



Kerry was arrested on suspicion of her murder and later re-arrested for the commission, preparation and commission of a terrorist act.

He was charged with one count of murder, the Crown Prosecution Service said on Monday evening.





Frank Ferguson, Chief Crown Prosecutor of the CPS Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said cops were still probing a potential political or terrorist connection.

“Our prosecutors have worked closely with the police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court, and we will continue working with them as their investigation progresses.”

Speaking from the steps of New Scotland Yard, assistant commissioner Laurence Taylor said they were not seeking anyone else and the investigation had been “extremely complex”.

The head of national counter terrorism policing offered his “deepest condolences to the family of Ann Widdecombe, and to everyone who knew and loved her”.



He said: “I know there has been significant interest in this case and rightly so, I want to make it very clear that our investigation into this individual, determining his motivations and any wider activity he may have been involved in, is continuing.”

He further said teams had received enough information for 800 lines of inquiry over the last week.

Kerry is set to appear in court Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday morning for his first hearing.



Forensic searches of his devices led terror cops to take over the probe, as they investigate whether the killing was politically motivated.

But the 28-year-old suspect “was not known” to the Prevent programme, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said.

Kerry has now been charged in connection with the veteran politician’s death, cops confirmed today.



It’s understood Ms Widdecombe’s domestic assistant found the Strictly star at her bungalow in Haytor, Dartmoor, on July 9.

The Reform UK spokeswoman is believed to have been bludgeoned to death in her isolated home at around 12.30pm the day before.

Ms Widdecombe’s final interview was recorded just minutes before she is believed to have been murdered.

CCTV footage obtained by The Sun showed Kerry leaving his home in Rotherham, South Yorks, just before 8am that day.



She had joined a Christian radio station between 11.54am and 12.10pm and defended Nigel Farage over a £5million gift which he says was for security.

Footage shows she recorded the interview in her library, wearing the same outfit as she wore in an appearance on TalkTV at 8am that morning.



Ms Widdecombe was then due to appear on Channel 5’s Matt Allwight show at 1pm – but failed to respond to show producers.

She did not reply to a Zoom link sent half an hour later at 12.48pm, before a producer messaged at 12.55pm asking: “Hi Ann is everything ok?”

During the show, Mr Allwright confirmed Ms Widdecombe had been due to appear but had stopped responding to messages.

Fears were raised for Ms Widdecombe, who was a regular on the panel show, and would typically respond to interview requests quickly.

However, the ex-MP failed to appear having not picked up the phone or joined a virtual link.



Studio staff reportedly made multiple further attempts to contact Ms Widdecombe over the following hours – but to no avail.

Channel 5 said it passed all of the relevant information to police after news of Ms Widdecombe’s death broke.

Presenter Dan Walker later confirmed her agent was contacted and asked to go check on her.

Her body was not found until 11.40am the next day, meaning there was a 24 hour gap in which the 78-year-old could not be contacted.



Cops were thought to be working on the theory she was murdered in a burglary gone wrong.

But counter terror cops later said they believe the murder was a “targeted attack”.

Ms Widdecombe’s home was shown on national television just five days before she was killed.

TV channel Quest aired an episode of Celebrity Yorkshire Auction House featuring the late 78-year-old politician on July 2, TV listings show.



In the episode, the inside of her £600,000 bungalow was shown in extensive detail as she gave host Angus Ashworth a guided tour.

There is no suggestion that visuals of the home on TV inspired or led to the killing.

Cops had initially arrested another man on Friday on suspicion of murder at an address in Newton Abbot, 11 miles away from her house.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But he was quickly released with no further action.

It is believed that her killer was caught on her home CCTV cameras.

News.title: Andy Burnham Cabinet picks – live: Rayner spotted at No10 after Miliband and Healey handed top jobs
News.content:
Andy Burnham has made several changes to his Cabinet — with the experienced John Healey, who quit recently under Keir Starmer's tenure, returning as Chancellor of the Exchequer

Andy Burnham has made his first Cabinet appointments — opting for John Healey as his Chancellor and Ed Miliband as Foreign Secretary.

Mr Healey replaces Rachel Reeves in the post with the latter confirming her departure from the Cabinet on social media this afternoon. David Lammy has also gone, vacating the deputy prime minister post, a role to which he was appointed by Keir Starmer last year.

Mr Miliband has been appointed Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs. He takes over from Yvette Cooper as Foreign Secretary in Mr Burnham's Cabinet. Mr Miliband, who also served as leader of the Labour Party from 2010 to 2015, was energy secretary in Mr Starmer's government. Ms Cooper herself is now Health Secretary, a position Wes Streeting held for nearly two years.

Other major figures from the Starmer era have been sacked, including Peter Kyle who was Business Secretary. His replacement is yet to be confirmed. Mr Healey, however, recently resigned as Mr Starmer’s defence secretary in a row over military funding.

But Shabana Mahmood has been reappointed Home Secretary by Mr Burnham. Ms Mahmood, MP for Ladywood, Birmingham, first took on the role in September 2025, replacing Ms Cooper in Mr Starmer's first reshuffle.

Talking today without a lectern or notes, in a huge move away from tradition, Mr Burnham, 56, spoke for 10 minutes and used the opportunity to outline his vision for the UK. He made several vows, stressing his first action will be to set out a plan to end rough sleeping. Minutes after this vow though, his Housing Secretary - Steve Reed OBE - quit.
