Sports.title: Keyshawn Fight Gives Haney More Leverage Than Shakur
Sports.content:
The purse bid also creates an awkward situation for Shakur. He has publicly welcomed a Haney-Keyshawn fight, but a Haney defeat may actually work against him. Shakur and Keyshawn have repeatedly referred to each other as brothers, making a fight between them look highly unlikely. If Keyshawn wins the title, one of Shakur’s biggest available opponents disappears.

A Devin victory leaves the door open for Shakur. Haney would remain champion, the fight would still carry championship stakes, and both fighters would have another reason to keep talking. Haney would also have little reason to accept a 144-pound handicap after successfully defending his title.

If Haney vacates instead, there is still no guarantee that the Shakur fight gets made. Ryan Garcia is tied up with Conor Benn, and Benn has already rejected the idea of accepting terms that favor Shakur. Ryan also has little reason to agree to another weight restriction after the disadvantage he dealt with against Gervonta Davis.

The purse bid puts Haney on the clock, but it also exposes a flaw in Shakur’s position. Haney has far more leverage by defending his title against Keyshawn than by surrendering it in hopes of landing a fight that has not been agreed to. If Shakur wants one of the biggest fights available, keeping Haney as a champion serves his interests far better than watching Keyshawn take the belt, who he refers to as his ‘brother’ and will never fight.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Gets IBF Eliminator Against Conor Wallace on October 3
Sports.content:
While Wallace holds the higher ranking, his record has been built almost entirely against regional-level opposition in Australia. The 30-year-old has yet to beat an established world contender despite spending eight years in the professional ranks. His biggest victories have come against fighters such as Jerome Pampellone and Dylan Colin, making it difficult to judge how he will perform against the most talented opponent of his career.

Whittaker has also been criticized for the level of his opposition as a professional, but he brings a much stronger amateur background into the eliminator. The Olympic silver medalist defeated several elite amateurs during his run to the 2020 Olympic final before losing to Cuba’s Arlen López in the gold medal bout. That experience against elite international competition gives him an advantage that Wallace does not possess.

If Bivol keeps hold of the IBF title, the winner will move into position for a championship fight under the sanctioning body’s rules.

This is a fight for Whittaker, 29, that should provide a clearer picture of his true standing among the global elite. Wallace’s ranking makes him a legitimate opponent, but his record leaves questions about how much resistance he can offer against a fighter with Whittaker’s amateur pedigree.

Sports.title: Barry Hearn Sees Different Anthony Joshua Before Prenga Fight
Sports.content:
“AJ is in an amazing place at the moment. Obviously, I’ve seen him since 2012. We’ve got very close. He’s like a member of our family. “I don’t think I’ve seen him so motivated for the long term. Some of that’s been fueled by that tragic accident, but he’s now talking about the next three years in the ring. It was a year ago that we were talking about potentially two fights and then go off to a happy retirement. “He’s very motivated; he feels good about himself, but boxing is a funny sport. It takes one punch from a big lad to knock out anyone in the world. So, you’ve got to be on your toes all the time. You can’t take this for granted. And when you get your chance, you’ve got to take it. “AJ is in the mood to cause a lot of pain on Saturday. I don’t think I’ve seen him look better than this in the 14 years I’ve known him. He is in the right place, and I think on Saturday in Jeddah will be the right time,” Barry Hearn told Sky Sports.

Prenga wasn’t chosen to be a threat. He’s there to give Joshua rounds after the accident. Gym performances don’t mean much when the opponent isn’t expected to test you. Until Joshua gets back in with a heavyweight who can crack and force him to answer questions, nobody knows if the flaws from the Dubois fight remain. Barry Hearn’s comments are what you’d expect from a promoter backing one of his biggest stars.

Joshua was stopped by Daniel Dubois in 2024. AJ rebounded from that defeat last December, knocking out the YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in a fight that was largely viewed as a celebrity-esque spectacle. Even in that victory, Joshua looked vulnerable before knocking out Paul.

AJ has always looked like a million bucks on the scale or hitting pads in the gym, but that means very little once someone real lands a clean shot on his chin.

He can look as motivated as Barry Hearn says, but gym work can’t replicate how a fighter reacts to getting hit, especially after coming back from a car accident. If Prenga manages to land something solid on Saturday, we’ll see right away if those old vulnerabilities are still there.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn: Boots Ennis Is ‘King Of The Castle’
Sports.content:
The way Hearn sees it, Vergil Jr. has nothing that Boots wants other than the money the fight would bring in. He doesn’t hold a major belt. The WBC interim 154-lb title isn’t enough.

Hearn says his fighter is no longer in the position of making concessions to land the bout. Boots is now “king of the castle.”

“He was taking the smaller side of the piece last time. He was going to be the B-side. He agreed to everything that they wanted to get that opportunity. So you imagine how he feels now that he’s king of the castle,” said Hearn to the media about Ennis’ position in negotiations with Vergil Ortiz Jr. “Vergil doesn’t have anything Boots wants other than a big fight and a big payday. What does Boots want to do now? He wants to unify.” “I don’t rule out that Ortiz fight at all. One thing is for sure. He ain’t close at all at the moment.“

Hearn’s comments reflect how much Ennis’ position has changed over the past year. During earlier discussions, Ennis was still chasing the biggest opportunities and was willing to accept B-side status to secure a fight with Ortiz. Hearn says those circumstances no longer exist.

Ennis now holds two world titles and has shifted his attention toward becoming the undisputed champion. Hearn indicated that unification bouts remain the priority, but he left the door open for Ortiz if Golden Boy presents an offer that outweighs Ennis’ other options.

“Tell us what the money is. And I’ll go to Jaron, and I’ll say, ‘We got Kelly, Fundora, or Ortiz,'” said Hearn.

Unless Turki Alalshikh gets involved, it’s questionable if a fight with Ortiz Jr. is financially appealing enough for Ennis to take time off from pursuing his goal of becoming the undisputed champion at junior middleweight.

Sports.title: Vernon Forrest Outboxes Shane Mosley Again in 2002 Rematch
Sports.content:
Six months after defeating Mosley to capture the championship, Forrest again relied on his size, jab and disciplined boxing to earn a 12-round unanimous decision and settle the rivalry once and for all.

The rematch carried enormous significance. Forrest defended both the WBC and Ring Magazine welterweight championships after taking them from Mosley in their first meeting earlier in the year in January 2002. Many believed Mosley would make the necessary adjustments and reclaim the titles, while Forrest had the opportunity to prove the upset had not been a one-night performance.

The event attracted 15,775 fans, the largest crowd to attend a boxing card in Indiana history at the time. HBO televised the championship bout nationally, and both fighters earned career-high paydays. Forrest received $3.42 million, while Mosley collected $2.8 million. Veteran referee Laurence Cole officiated the 12-round title fight.

Mosley came out aggressively, looking to erase the disappointment of the first bout by forcing exchanges from the opening bell. Forrest refused to be drawn into a firefight. Standing three inches taller with the longer reach, he established his jab early, circled effectively and answered Mosley’s rushes with sharp counters before tying him up whenever the action moved inside.

As the rounds progressed, Forrest steadily took control. Forrest repeatedly stabbed Mosley with the jab before tying him up whenever the challenger got close, forcing Mosley to reset his offense over and over. Referee Laurence Cole was forced to separate the fighters throughout the contest as the tactical battle became increasingly physical.

The middle rounds lacked sustained action, drawing boos from portions of the crowd, but Forrest remained committed to the game plan. One report even noted that a fight in the stands during the sixth round briefly attracted as much attention as the action inside the ring.

Mosley increased the pressure during the championship rounds, finally producing several spirited exchanges in the tenth. Forrest answered with crisp counterpunching and finished strongly, landing several hard right hands late in the eleventh before boxing confidently through the final round. There were no knockdowns, but Forrest consistently landed the cleaner, more effective punches.

CompuBox statistics reflected the tactical nature of the contest. Forrest landed 120 of 446 punches, while Mosley connected on 114 of 259, with Forrest’s jab, timing and ring control outweighing Mosley’s higher connect percentage.

Judges Gary Merritt (117-111), Tony Castellano (116-112) and Jerry Roth (115-113) all favored Forrest. HBO unofficial scorer Harold Lederman and several media scorecards also had Forrest winning, confirming that his first victory had been no accident.

The rematch closed the book on one of the era’s most compelling rivalries. Forrest had defeated Mosley twice as a professional after also beating him during the 1992 U.S. Olympic Trials, establishing a rare mastery over one of boxing’s greatest fighters.

Mosley later captured world titles in higher weight classes, while Forrest continued his championship run before unifying the welterweight division. More than two decades later, the rematch remains one of the signature victories of Forrest’s Hall of Fame career, removing any doubt that his success against Mosley was built on superior technique rather than surprise.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Reveals Zuffa Promise Behind His Signing
Sports.content:
Shakur is counting on the Tank and Devin Haney fights happening for him, but they may not. If the Haney and Tank Davis matchups evaporate, the entire situation changes, and Shakur’s massive money-making leverage shrinks instantly.

Even under the best circumstances, it’s not a given that Zuffa will be able to hook a big fish like Gervonta Davis to fight Shakur. Despite Shakur’s elite skills and massive new Zuffa backing, he simply doesn’t move the needle the same way with the casual audience.

If Shakur demands anything close to parity or tries to dictate the terms, Tank will likely dig his heels in. Tank has shown before that he would rather sit out, pursue a lesser name, or even talk about walking away from the sport entirely than give up his leverage to an opponent he feels needs him more than he needs them.

“What really went into the decision was mainly life-changing money. Not only life-changing money, just life-changing opportunities,” Shakur said to Fighthype. “Dana [White] and Nick [Khan], they kept saying, ‘We want to get you in with the best fighters. We wanted you to fight the best.’ The guys that they mentioned was Devin and Tank. And when I heard that, I’m like, why would I go away from what I’ve been wanting to do my whole career? I think my whole career I’ve been saying the titles and all that, I done it. With all due respect to the titles, I appreciate y’all… but I want to fight the best. I want to get in there and prove myself and get under them bright lights and see who’s the best. I’m not scared of taking no risk.”

Haney hasn’t said whether he’s going to fight Shakur next or defend against his WBO mandatory, Keyshawn Davis. If Keyshawn actually upsets Haney to take the WBO welterweight title, Shakur’s biggest potential fight is effectively dead.

“I think that’s what really kind of kicked it off with me and Zuffa. Their vision is as big as mine. I ain’t never really hear promoters with big visions like me. It’s an amazing thing, and I’m happy to be the person to lead the new school and new generation,” Shakur said.

With Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn officially locked in for September 12, a Ryan loss changes everything for the 147-pound division. Ryan is arguably the sport’s biggest ticket seller and pay-per-view draw outside of Canelo. Shakur vs. Ryan is a massive financial fallback if Tank or Haney fall through. If Benn beats Ryan, that golden parachute disappears.

While a Benn victory makes Conor a massive star under the Zuffa banner, a Shakur vs. Benn fight doesn’t carry the same casual fan appeal or domestic PPV weight as a clash with Garcia. Benn doesn’t have the same popularity in the U.S as he does in the UK. American fans view Benn as the son of a famous retired ex-world champion, who has never beaten any elite-level fighters during his career.

Sports.title: Mike McCallum Flattens Donald Curry With Devastating Left Hook
Sports.content:
Many favored Curry’s speed and sharper boxing to carry him to another world championship. Instead, one perfectly timed punch produced one of the greatest knockouts of the decade.

The scheduled 15-round championship bout was televised by HBO from the Caesars Palace Sports Pavilion in Paradise, Nevada. Richard Steele served as referee, while Guy Jutras, Jerry Roth and Ove Ovesen handled the scoring. An official attendance figure was never widely reported, but the event drew major attention as one of the biggest championship fights of 1987.

McCallum was making the sixth defense of the WBA junior middleweight title he had won in 1984. Nicknamed “The Body Snatcher,” the Jamaican-born master tactician had knocked out every opponent during his title reign. Even with those accomplishments, sportsbooks installed him as a 2-1 underdog.

Curry entered as the WBA’s top contender after previously holding the WBA, WBC, IBF and Ring Magazine welterweight championships. Moving to 154 pounds offered a fresh opportunity to reestablish himself among boxing’s elite and position himself for even bigger fights.

The fight also carried significant financial rewards. McCallum earned a reported $475,000, while Curry received $425,000, excellent purses for championship fighters during that era.

For four rounds, the betting odds appeared justified. Curry’s jab repeatedly beat McCallum to the target. His hand speed, combinations and movement kept the champion from settling into his rhythm, and a sharp right hand in the second round buckled McCallum’s knees. By the end of the fourth, Curry had built a comfortable lead on all three scorecards. McCallum remained dangerous, but he looked a step behind as Curry controlled the action.

At 1:14 into Round 5, Curry stepped inside and drove a right hand toward McCallum’s body. McCallum anticipated the attack, gave a subtle body feint of his own, then unleashed a crushing left hook that landed flush on Curry’s jaw. The fight ended instantly.

Curry crashed flat onto his back, staring toward the lights as Steele began the count. He slowly regained awareness around seven but never gathered himself in time to continue. The referee completed the count, and McCallum had retained his championship with one of boxing’s most unforgettable single punches.

The knockout earned KO Magazine’s Knockout of the Year honors and remains one of the finest one-punch finishes ever shown on HBO. Ironically, Sugar Ray Leonard worked the broadcast that night after Curry had reportedly objected to his presence on the telecast, which brought an extra bit of drama to an already memorable evening.

McCallum later vacated the WBA title to pursue championships at middleweight and light heavyweight, eventually becoming a three-division world champion and earning induction into the International Boxing Hall of Fame. Although he never landed the marquee fights against Sugar Ray Leonard, Marvin Hagler, Thomas Hearns or Roberto Durán, his body of work cemented his reputation as one of boxing’s most accomplished champions.

The defeat for Curry proved far more damaging than anyone expected. He won a handful of fights afterward but never returned to the level that once made him one of the sport’s pound-for-pound stars, suffering later defeats to Michael Nunn and Terry Norris before retiring.

More than three decades later, McCallum’s left hook remains one of the greatest one-punch knockouts in championship boxing history and the defining moment of an unforgettable title fight.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Pressures Diego Pacheco to Fight Lester Martinez
Sports.content:
“It’s time to grab a hold of them balls, bro. You should have been handling Sheeraz. I was picking you to beat Sheeraz. Sheeraz is getting better and better while your ass is sitting back here fighting against dudes like Aleem,” said Bradley on his YouTube channel. “Why don’t you go ahead and go after Berlanga after this? Better yet, go ahead and get Lester. Lester fought this dude, and we’re comparing the two. Lester went the full distance with him. You got him up out of there. Why don’t you fight Lester? That’s a hell of a fight.”

Bradley is right that Pacheco needs a real test, but Saturday’s performance didn’t convince me he’s ready for the division’s elite. He boxed well, finished Aleem impressively and showed patience under Buddy McGirt, yet he was still getting hit too often by a fighter who isn’t known as a devastating puncher. That’s the concern.

If Aleem was able to land that frequently, what happens against Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez or even middleweights Carlos Adames or Yoenli Hernandez if they moved up? Those fighters carry more power, are physically stronger, and wouldn’t be as forgiving once Pacheco found himself exchanging at close range.

The Kevin Lele Sadjo fight exposed flaws in Pacheco when the action became physical. He didn’t look comfortable under sustained pressure, and those issues weren’t answered against Aleem because the matchup never forced him into the same type of fight.

Pacheco’s post-fight comments focused on Canelo Alvarez and Jaime Munguia. Eddie Hearn has also floated Munguia as a possible next opponent. If Matchroom wants to prove Pacheco belongs with the division’s elite, fights against Iglesias, Lester, Adames or Hernandez would answer far more questions than a quick jump toward a lucrative name.

Hearn has the financial backing to make those fights. If Matchroom bypasses them and heads straight toward Munguia, it will be difficult to ignore the possibility that the priority is maximizing Pacheco’s value before a dangerous contender exposes the flaws that are still visible in his game.

Ghana News.title: NPA rejects claims of financial loss in Auditor-General’s report
Ghana News.content:
The National Petroleum Authority (NPA) has dismissed media reports suggesting that the Auditor-General’s recent Performance Audit Report uncovered financial losses, corruption or misappropriation within the Authority, insisting that such claims do not reflect the contents of the audit.

In a statement issued on Monday, July 20, the NPA said the Auditor-General’s Performance Audit Report on its operations covering the period from 2023 to 2025 did not establish any financial loss or revenue loss to the Authority.

It stressed that media characterisations describing the report as evidence of “rot”, corruption or financial impropriety were not findings contained in the audit.

The Authority also criticised a publication by The NewsCenta newspaper, stating that the report failed to include management’s responses to the Auditor-General’s findings. According to the NPA, omitting its official response presented an incomplete picture of the audit outcomes.

Reaffirming its commitment to transparency, accountability and sound corporate governance, the Authority said it would continue to work constructively with the Ghana Audit Service.

It added that it would implement appropriate recommendations from the audit to strengthen regulatory oversight, improve operational efficiency and enhance consumer protection in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector.

The NPA further urged the public to rely only on its official communications regarding the matter, assuring stakeholders of its continued commitment to maintaining high standards of governance and effective regulation within the petroleum industry.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t to build new Community Day SHSs in Nima, Ayawaso and Kasoa – Education Minister
Ghana News.content:
Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu

The government is planning to establish more Community Day Senior High Schools (SHSs) in selected peri-urban communities as part of efforts to expand access to secondary education.

Minister for Education Haruna Iddrisu disclosed this during the Government Accountability Series in Accra on Monday, July 20, saying the initiative is being supported by the $300 million Transformative Secondary Education for Access, Results and Relevance for Jobs (STARR-J) Project.

In June 2026, the World Bank approved IDA financing of US$300 million for the STARR-J Project, which will expand access to quality secondary education and equip more young people with the basic knowledge and skills necessary to transition to higher education and enter the labour market.

The minister said President John Dramani Mahama has consistently advocated for the expansion of Community Day Senior High Schools to bring quality secondary education closer to communities.

Mr Iddrisu revealed that the government is considering the construction of new Community Day SHSs in areas including Nima, Ayawaso and Kasoa.

According to him, the new schools will be modelled after the Dome-Kwabenya Community Day Senior High School, which was established to provide more opportunities for students within its catchment area.

"It is the view of President Mahama that we should encourage the establishment of community day care schools in the category of what is in Kwabenya. So we will build one of those in Nima, Ayawaso, and one in Kasoa as part of the STARR-J Project," he said.

He explained that the move forms part of the government's broader strategy to address infrastructure gaps in the second-cycle education sector, improve access, and support the sustainability of the Free Senior High School programme.

Ghana News.title: Minority challenges High Court ruling against Wontumi
Ghana News.content:
Alexander Afenyo-Markin

The Minority Caucus in Parliament has raised sharp constitutional objections to the 20-year prison sentence handed down to the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, describing the verdict as a miscarriage of justice.

In a judgment delivered by Justice Audrey Kocuvie-Tay at the High Court in Accra, Chairman Wontumi and his firm, Akonta Mining Limited, were convicted on two counts each under the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), as amended.

However, in a press statement issued on Monday, 20 July 2026, and signed by Minority Leader Osahen Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin, the Minority Caucus alleged procedural irregularities and selective prosecution, vowing to test the decision at the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court.

Denial of counsel, comparison with Tsatsu Tsikata case

A primary grievance raised by the Minority is the trial court's decision to deliver judgment in the absence of Wontumi’s lead counsel, who had formally notified the court of a pre-existing professional commitment outside the jurisdiction.

The caucus argued that proceeding to sentence the accused without his chosen defense representation infringed upon Article 19(2)(g) of the 1992 Constitution, which guarantees an accused person the right to be defended by a lawyer of their own choice.

Drawing historical parallels, the Minority referenced the landmark case of Tsatsu Tsikata, whose 2008 conviction was eventually overturned by the Court of Appeal on 30 November 2016. The appellate court ruled that the trial judge's decision to proceed while higher court questions remained unresolved constituted a miscarriage of justice.

"If the right to counsel of choice mattered in 2003, it matters in 2026, and it matters exactly as much when the accused sits on the other side of the political aisle," the statement emphasized.

Constitutional referral refusal

The Minority further faulted Justice Kocuvie-Tay for refusing the defense team's application to refer constitutional interpretation questions regarding Section 99(2)(b) of Act 703 to the Supreme Court under Article 130.

Relying on the precedent set in Republic v. The High Court, General Jurisdiction 6, Accra; Ex Parte Dr. Zanetor A. Rawlings (2016), the caucus insisted that a lower court judge errs by deciding that a statutory provision is "clear and unambiguous" to avoid referring it, as interpreting the Constitution remains the exclusive purview of the apex court.

The statement added that lifting Akonta Mining Limited's corporate veil to hold Wontumi personally liable represented an exceptional legal remedy that required closer appellate scrutiny.

Allegations of selective justice

While reiterating its support for the national fight against illegal mining (galamsey), the Minority accused state prosecutors of applying a double standard based on political affiliation.

They questioned the lack of prosecutorial progress regarding an investigation ordered on 15 July 2025 by Attorney-General Dr. Dominic Akuritinga Ayine into National Organiser Joseph Yamin and National Vice Chairman Yakubu Abanga over alleged galamsey activities.

The caucus also cited an unprosecuted takeover of a licensed concession at Apinto involving foreign nationals, contrasting those delays with the swift trial and heavy custodial sentence handed to the opposition regional chairman.

Calls for transparency and appeal

The Minority Caucus concluded by demanding that the Office of the Attorney-General publish its full enforcement record on illegal mining across the political spectrum.

Urging Wontumi's legal team to pursue certiorari and appellate remedies, the caucus assured NPP members in the Ashanti Region and across the diaspora of their commitment to challenging the conviction through all constitutional channels.

Ghana News.title: Ashanti Caucus NPP MPs rally behind Wontumi after conviction
Ghana News.content:
Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi

The Ashanti Caucus of New Patriotic Party (NPP) Members of Parliament has thrown its weight behind the regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, following his conviction and 20-year prison sentence in an illegal mining case.

In a statement issued on Monday, the caucus expressed "unwavering solidarity" with Chairman Wontumi, describing him as a fearless and selfless leader whose contributions to the growth of the NPP cannot be diminished by the court's decision.

"Chairman Wontumi has, over the years, distinguished himself as a fearless, resilient, and selfless leader whose sacrifices and commitment have significantly strengthened the New Patriotic Party in the Ashanti Region and across Ghana," the statement said.

Chairman Wontumi is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence after being convicted by the High Court in connection with illegal mining activities involving Akonta Mining Limited.

While reaffirming its respect for the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary, the caucus said it remains confident that the appellate process would overturn the conviction.

The MPs noted that every Ghanaian has a constitutional right to challenge judicial decisions and insisted that the judgment should not be regarded as the end of Wontumi's political career.

"We reject every attempt to portray this judgment as the end of Chairman Wontumi's public and political life. If anything, this moment should strengthen the resolve of every patriotic member of our Party to rally behind a man who has consistently stood firmly for the ideals of the NPP," the statement added.

The caucus also raised concerns over what it described as a growing perception of selective justice in the country's anti-illegal mining campaign.

According to the MPs, the fight against illegality must be conducted fairly and without political considerations, warning against using the justice system to settle political scores.

"The fight against illegality must be fair, impartial, and devoid of political considerations. Justice must never become an instrument for settling political scores or intimidating political opponents," the statement said.

The Ashanti Caucus further appealed to NPP supporters, particularly those in the Ashanti Region, to remain calm and united while the party pursues an appeal against the judgment.

It assured Chairman Wontumi that he would not face the legal battle alone.

"Stay strong. Stay resolute. The Ashanti Caucus stands firmly with you. This battle is not yours alone; it is a test of our collective commitment to justice, fairness, and democratic principles," the statement concluded.

Ghana News.title: D.O.O.R. Initiative projects $8bn diaspora investment to drive Ghana’s economic growth
Ghana News.content:
The Decade of Our Own Return (D.O.O.R.) Initiative has renewed its call on Africans in the diaspora to reconnect with Ghana through investment, permanent settlement and skills transfer, with organisers projecting at least $8 billion in economic activity during the programme's first year.

Speaking at the media launch of the Open Door Dialogue, founder of the D.O.O.R. Initiative, Dr Obenfo Obádélé Kambon, said the 10-year programme seeks to reverse the trend of Ghanaians leaving the country in search of opportunities by attracting members of the African diaspora to relocate, establish businesses and contribute to national development.

Founder of the D.O.O.R. Initiative, Dr Obenfo Obádélé Kambon

He explained that the initiative is designed for people of African descent worldwide, including descendants of those displaced through the trans-Atlantic slave trade and Africans living abroad, encouraging them to invest, transfer skills and create employment opportunities in Ghana.

According to Dr Kambon, the initiative builds on the momentum created by Ghana's Year of Return and Beyond the Return campaigns but shifts the focus from heritage tourism to long-term repatriation, entrepreneurship and sustainable economic development.

"As it stands right now, the first year of the Decade of Our Own Return, those in the diaspora—these are Ghanaians doing remittances, those are historic diasporans who have come to live—the baseline number is $8 billion," he said.

"I think we can do a lot in Ghana with $8 billion. Every single sector stands to benefit. That's in terms of agriculture, hospitality, real estate, mining and every single aspect of Ghanaian society can be impacted greatly by what diasporans are doing."

Ghana's Special Envoy to the Caribbean Region, Kwasi Kyei Darkwah, also appealed to members of the diaspora to see investing in Ghana as both an opportunity and a responsibility.

"We don't have it all. We are still working hard to make it here in Ghana," he said.

"Many of us who have lived abroad and determined that we want to come back home and work here, I don't call it a sacrifice. I call it a duty and a responsibility."

He said Africans living abroad possess the financial resources, expertise and international networks needed to help accelerate Ghana's development and strengthen economic growth.

A member of the Open Door Dialogue committee, Dr Sarah Dorgbadzi, urged young Ghanaians to believe in the opportunities available within the country rather than pursuing uncertain futures abroad.

"We need our young people to understand that opportunities exist here," she said.

"They don't have to go and be second- or third-class citizens in other places."

She added that stronger collaboration between local professionals and Africans in the diaspora could stimulate entrepreneurship, create jobs and support national development.

The D.O.O.R. Initiative aims to position Ghana as a preferred destination for Africans in the diaspora seeking to return permanently, acquire property, establish businesses and contribute to the country's economic transformation.

Through the Open Door Dialogue, organisers hope to strengthen partnerships between government, the private sector, civil society and the global African community to ensure that diaspora engagement delivers lasting economic and social benefits.

They believe sustained investment and repatriation can help position Ghana not only as a place of historical reconnection but also as a destination where Africans in the diaspora can build businesses, create wealth and leave a lasting legacy.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi was bound to be convicted after prosecution witness’ testimony – Martin Kpebu
Ghana News.content:
Martin Kpebu

Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu says the conviction of New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, was inevitable given the evidence presented during the trial.

Speaking on Joy FM's Top Story on Monday, July 20, Mr Kpebu said the testimony of the second prosecution witness, proved decisive because he admitted carrying out the mining activities and testified that Chairman Wontumi had given him access to the concession.

"The person who was given the opportunity to do the galamsey came to testify as the second prosecution witness. He did the galamsey and testified that Chairman Wontumi gave him the land to mine," he explained.

Mr Kpebu said that because the mining activities were not authorised, they constituted illegal mining, making the evidence particularly damaging to the defence.

"Once the gentleman who did the actual mining operations is testifying against Wontumi, and there is no evidence to discredit him or suggest he was lying or acting out of ulterior motives, Wontumi was bound to be convicted," he stated.

He argued that the outcome of the case should not have come as a surprise, describing it as "an open and shut case" based on the evidence before the court.

"This day was always coming. Wontumi himself would have known that conviction was a possibility because of the evidence that had been laid," he said.

Mr Kpebu's comments come after the Accra High Court sentenced Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

However, the New Patriotic Party believes the conviction is a political and vowed to appeal.

Ghana News.title: Ho to get modern special needs school under $300m STARR-J project – Education Minister
Ghana News.content:
Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu

The Volta Regional capital, Ho, is set to benefit from a new modern school for learners with special needs under the government's $300 million Transformative Secondary Education for Access, Results and Relevance for Jobs (STARR-J) Project.

Minister for Education Haruna Iddrisu announced this while addressing the Government Accountability Series in Accra on Monday, July 20.

"I am also happy to note that under the STARR-J Project, Ho and the Volta region will benefit from a new special needs education facility to support learners with disabilities in that area," he said.

"The second location for the second special needs school is now debated with data between Kintapo and another town in the Upper East Region. If it is possible, we will probably consider and do it all," he added.

He said the project reflects the government's commitment to improving access to quality education for persons with disabilities and ensuring that learners with special needs are not left behind.

According to the minister, the planned facility will provide a modern learning environment tailored to the needs of students with disabilities, as part of broader efforts to strengthen inclusive education across the country.

Mr Iddrisu stressed that the government remains committed to investing in the welfare and education of persons with special needs, describing the proposed school as a significant step towards promoting equitable access to education.

In June 2026, the World Bank approved IDA financing of US$300 million for the Ghana Secondary Education Transformation for Access, Relevance, and Results for Jobs (STARR-J) Project, which will expand access to quality secondary education and equip more young people with the basic knowledge and skills necessary to transition to higher education and enter the labour market.

Ghana News.title: Martin Kpebu sees no strong grounds to overturn Wontumi’s conviction
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has expressed doubts about the prospects of an appeal by the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako (Chairman Wontumi), following his conviction and 20-year prison sentence.

Speaking on Joy FM's News Night on Monday, July 20, Mr Kpebu said, in his assessment of the case, he had not identified any compelling legal grounds that could lead an appellate court to overturn the High Court's decision.

Chairman Wontumi was sentenced to 20 years' imprisonment after being convicted by the High Court in connection with illegal mining activities. His legal team has indicated its intention to appeal the decision, while the NPP has maintained that the conviction was unsupported by the evidence and should be overturned by the appellate courts.

Mr Kpebu's comments come after the NPP announced plans to challenge the conviction, describing the judgment as a "travesty of justice" and insisting the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

Mr Kpebu, however, said his reading of the case pointed in a different direction.

"This one, maybe I have a biased mind. It's difficult. It's difficult to really appreciate and come out with a strong ground of appeal for Wontumi," he said.

"I think I see it as a one-way street, and in this one, he (Chairman Wontumi) is guilty as charged."

The legal practitioner acknowledged that lawyers often approach cases differently when acting for a client but indicated that, based on his current assessment, he could not identify a convincing basis for reversing the conviction.

Mr Kpebu further disclosed that he would not have accepted instructions to represent Chairman Wontumi because he had previously been involved in efforts to have allegations against him investigated.

"I can never even be a lawyer on his side, no. Because, you know, we had earlier on presented a petition against him."

According to him, a petition, which he said was filed in 2022 during the Akufo-Addo administration, has yet to be conclusively dealt with.

Mr Kpebu alleged that the matter did not receive the necessary attention at the time because of the NPP regional chairman's political influence.

"Our petition has been pending since 2022. That was in the Akufo-Addo administration, and it's because of Wontumi's political power, immense political power; the CID office at the time didn't do much about it because of the obvious political influence."

He stressed that his previous involvement in the matter informed his perspective on the case and his assessment of the likelihood of a successful appeal.

"So you see that because I'm not on Wontumi's side, I can't really see what grounds of appeal I would do for him. I mean, you said a strong one. You didn't say what grounds can be formulated, but you meant a strong one. So I'm looking at what can get him free. I don't see one."

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Protests in Italy after Moroccan man dies during arrest
World.content:
Outrage across Italy’s political spectrum following death in Bologna likened to killing of George Floyd in 2020.

Click here to share on social media

Demonstrations have been held in the northern Italian city of Bologna after a Moroccan man died while being restrained by police.

Hundreds rallied on Monday evening amid a fierce political row over the officers’ conduct. The death of Abderrahim Fakir on Sunday has drawn inevitable comparisons to the killing of George Floyd by United States police in Minneapolis in 2020.

Demonstrators knelt with raised fists on Sunday, a gesture associated with the Black Lives Matter movement. Further protests, backed by the city’s mayor and major trade unions, were held on Monday evening.

The 42-year-old Moroccan entrepreneur died when police detained him following reports of aggressive behaviour.

Video of the incident, filmed by a local resident and widely shared online, has prompted demands from opposition figures for accountability. Leaders of the right-wing government have defended the officers involved.

The video shows Fakir face down on the ground as two officers restrain him. He repeatedly calls out “help, help, that’s enough” before falling silent.

Police then bind his ankles and only afterwards check his vital signs.

According to media reports, officers had used pepper spray and held him down while trying to handcuff him after he reacted aggressively.

“My brother had asked for help… and they killed him,” one of Fakir’s brothers told the Corriere Della Sera newspaper.

Bologna prosecutors have opened an inquiry under a newly introduced legal procedure and requested bodycam video from the officers involved.



The far-right Deputy Prime Minister, Matteo Salvini, and other government allies have praised the officers’ conduct.

Opposition figures have accused Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s coalition of fostering a climate of hostility.

Centre-left legislator Francesco Boccia warned against Italy adopting an “ICE model” of US policing.
