World.title: Judge puts temporary pause on Paramount-Warner merger
World.content:
Paramount Skydance’s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery hit a roadblock Monday after a federal judge temporarily paused the proposed merger, granting a request from a coalition of 12 state attorneys general who sued to thwart the $110 billion deal.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín of the Northern District of California issued a temporary restraining order barring Paramount from closing the transaction, a corporate tie-up that would unite two movie studios, two streaming platforms and two news organizations under the control of David Ellison, the son of billionaire technology tycoon Larry Ellison.

Martínez-Olguín’s order said the restraining order will remain in effect for 14 days. The judge, who is presiding over the case, scheduled an Aug. 3 hearing on the states’ motion for a preliminary injunction, which would freeze the transaction while the legal process plays out.

The plaintiffs, led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, sued to block the merger July 13, arguing in a 38-page complaint that it would “extinguish competition” in Hollywood.

“The unlawful merger of these two entertainment behemoths would lead to higher prices, lower quality, and less content for film and television, harming movie theaters, basic cable distributors, and ultimately, audiences on every sofa and movie theater seat in the U.S.,” Bonta said in a statement accompanying the court filing.

Bonta and his fellow Democratic attorneys general contend that the transaction violates Section 7 of the Clayton Antitrust Act of 1914, a federal law that bars mergers likely to substantially lessen competition.

01:30 Paramount-Warner merger could impact entertainment options 00:00 00:00

The states argue the deal would reduce competition in three areas: wide-release theatrical film distribution, anticipated top-grossing movie distribution, and the market for distributing basic cable channels to cable and satellite providers.

Paramount has forcefully pushed back on those claims, arguing that the states’ crusade is “wrong on both the facts and the law” and blasting the restraining order bid as “one of the weakest merger challenges in modern antitrust history.”

In response to a request for comment on the temporary restraining order, a Paramount spokesperson said in part: “We are confident the evidence will demonstrate that the State AGs’ antitrust arguments are without merit as their alleged markets and claims of anticompetitive effects are without any basis in modern market realities.”

The company has already received regulatory clearance from the Justice Department, and it has touted similar approvals from other countries, including Australia and China.

“We will vigorously defend the transaction and demonstrate that this challenge is inconsistent with sound competition policy and the competitive realities of the media marketplace,” Paramount said in a statement.

Paramount executives are motivated to close the deal soon. That’s partly because the company agreed to pay Warner Bros. shareholders a “ticking fee” of 25 cents a share each quarter if the transaction isn’t wrapped up by Sept. 30.

The potential penalty is worth more than $600 million per quarter.

Paramount owns a 114-year-old film studio, the Paramount+ streaming service, the CBS broadcast network, and a suite of cable assets that includes MTV and Nickelodeon. Warner Bros. owns a 116-year-old film studio, the cable brands CNN and HBO, and popular intellectual property such as the Batman and Superman franchises.

The state-driven lawsuit is the most significant threat to the deal since it was inked, though it is not the only hurdle standing in Paramount’s way. The European Union’s antitrust arm is reviewing the transaction, and the British culture secretary recently said she was “minded to intervene” in the deal, citing concerns about concentrated ownership of media enterprises.

The merger has also drawn opposition from organized labor and a group of consumers.

The Writers Guild of America filed its own antitrust suit, arguing that the deal would suppress members’ wages and shrink the number of available jobs. Separately, a group of consumers filed an antitrust suit focused on the harms of combining Paramount+ and HBO Max. (Martínez-Olguín denied the consumer plaintiffs’ request for a preliminary injunction to freeze the merger.)

In the states’ antitrust case, California’s Bonta was joined by the attorneys general of Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico and Oregon. New York Attorney General Letitia James has said the merger “threatens to raise costs for consumers and put jobs and businesses nationwide at risk.”

The proposed deal has a political dimension. Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison is an ally of President Donald Trump. Trump has praised the Ellison family and publicly called for new ownership of CNN. “We’re trying to have CNN go in a normal path,” Trump recently told the network’s Jake Tapper in an on-air phone interview.

The younger Ellison has already embarked on sweeping changes at CBS News, hiring opinion journalist Bari Weiss to overhaul “60 Minutes” and the network’s evening news broadcast.

World.title: FDA says it’s still investigating Taylor Farms in cyclosporiasis outbreak
World.content:
Taylor Farms continues to be the subject of a Food and Drug Administration investigation into the growing cyclosporiasis outbreak, despite a false positive test result, the agency said Monday.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Late Sunday, the FDA said that a lettuce sample from the company had falsely tested positive for cyclospora, the parasite that causes the illness. That sample, however, did not come from lettuce already implicated in the outbreak and recall. Instead, it came from a separate shipment the agency collected during routine import inspections.

“To clarify, this false-positive lab sample DOES NOT change the basis for FDA’s ongoing outbreak investigation or the overwhelming epidemiological data supporting the current voluntary recall by Taylor Farms,” the FDA said Monday on X.

The company’s voluntary recall of shredded iceberg lettuce to 27 states is still in effect.

On Sunday, Taylor Farms said in a statement that the FDA had “apologized” about the false positive test results. On a call Monday, an FDA official disputed Taylor Farms’ claim that the agency had issued an official apology.

Taylor Farms did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Determining the source of an outbreak goes beyond finding a positive sample.

Public health officials don’t rely solely on laboratory tests to identify the source of a foodborne outbreak, said Donald Schaffner, a food microbiology professor and chair of the food science department at Rutgers University.

Instead, investigators look at patient samples and interviews, food receipts and information from the food supply chain to determine where the contaminated food likely came from.

In the ongoing outbreak, investigators found that many people who got sick had eaten at Taco Bell restaurants supplied with Taylor Farms lettuce. As of Saturday, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention had confirmed more than 1,600 cases in people in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia.

“Taylor Farms is still implicated because of the epidemiology,” Schaffner wrote in an email. “This means that people that ate at Taco Bell, and ate Taylor Farm lettuce, are sick with the parasite. It’s important to realize that this is only a statistical correlation. Correlation is not causation, but it was strong enough evidence that FDA and CDC believe that this is the cause.”

On Saturday, Taco Bell said it had removed all Taylor Farms lettuce from its U.S. restaurants.

Schaffner said it’s unusual for investigators to be able to detect the cyclospora parasite in a food sample.

“Almost always it’s too late because the food has already spoiled or has been eaten,” he said.

A positive result for the parasite would have been a strong piece of confirmatory data, said Don Stoeckel, an environmental microbiologist and associate at the Produce Safety Alliance, a food safety training group.

The lack of a positive result, however, “does not reduce the importance of following the CDC’s recommendation to avoid consumption of the product named on the CDC investigations page,” Stoeckel said.

World.title: A look at the most exciting moments from the 2026 FIFA World Cup
World.content:
The 2026 World Cup has come to a close.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Spain is the winner after a thrilling 1-0 win in the final, holding off Lionel Messi and Argentina from winning a second consecutive title.

The tournament began on June 11 with the opening match in Mexico, before play extended to the United States and Canada. It was an exciting tournament overall, as well as the first to feature 48 teams.

New heroes — such as Cape Verde’s goalkeeper Vozinha — were created, while several of the sport’s legends — such as Messi and France’s Kylian Mbappé — continued putting their stamp on the world’s biggest stage.

Here’s a look back at the tournament through some of the NBC News photo team’s favorite images, featuring unique atmospheres, raucous fans, the most memorable moments and more.

World.title: The soccer fans who fell in love with America during the World Cup
World.content:
The 2026 World Cup was an undeniable sensation in the United States, setting records for television ratings while millions of fans piled into stadiums to take in all the action.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

What happened off the field was arguably just as exciting, as people from all over the world traveled to the U.S. not only to watch their favorite teams and players perform, but to engage in a cultural exchange with Americans.

Follow along for live coverage.

With the World Cup coming to a close with Sunday’s final, here are some of the best off-the-pitch moments from the summer tournament.

The love affair between Algeria and Kansas City

Kansas City was the smallest host city in the United States, but that didn’t stop Algerian fans from having a big party in the Midwest. Kansas City hosted a group match between Argentina and Algeria, which drew fans from both countries into a city with a population of a little over 500,000.

The Algerian contingent seemed especially happy with their trip, with many also enjoying their time in nearby Lawrence, Kansas.

“A lot of people don’t even know Algeria exists. And it’s the same for us. We had never heard of Lawrence until the Algerian team came here. The people were very, very welcoming, and they adopted the Algerian team,” Hanafi Habbas told NBC affiliate KSHB in Kansas City.

David Sauter, who runs a local T-shirt printing shop in Lawrence, said his sales exceeded his typical Christmas figures.

“It has been so wonderful how everyone here has just been open with open arms, welcoming people. The Algerians have been amazing,” Sauter said.

The ‘Viking Row’ becomes a sensation

Playing in the World Cup for the first time in 28 years, Norway quickly endeared itself to the greater soccer community thanks to its now-infamous “Viking Row” celebration.

Mimicking a group of Vikings in a longboat, Norwegian fans typically do the celebration while seated at a match, chanting “Row!” as they pull imaginary oars to the beat of a drum.

During the World Cup, Norway’s fans brought the celebration everywhere, including a New York Mets game at Citi Field, Times Square and even an escalator in Boston. Norway’s team finally got in on the fun, doing their own row after a 3-2 win over Senegal in the group stage.

“It’s about rowing for the team,” Ole Frøystad, the fan credited with popularizing the celebration, told NBC News. “Making sure that we get the team to feel good on the pitch, make them perform the way that they should, and just support them in every way that we can.”

Everybody loves ranch dressing

Of all the American foods that caught on with foreigners during the World Cup — from gas stations like Buc-ees to diners like Waffle House — perhaps no singular item excited soccer fans as much as ranch dressing.

Ranch appeared to take the World Cup by storm, at one point even drawing a response from the TSA, which playfully warned fans about bringing bottles out of the country.

The Tartan Army takeover

Scotland’s soccer fans, known as the Tartan Army, made their presence felt during the World Cup in cities such as Boston and Miami.

In Miami, thousands of Scottish fans marched from a local bar to a Miami Marlins baseball game, bringing with them their signature kilts and bagpipes.

Most memorably, in Boston, the Tartan Army partied so hard it started drinking bars dry. The company behind the beer Sam Adams told NBC Boston its Boston Taproom ran out of Samuel Adams Boston Lager one weekend because of the Tartan Army, which drank four times as much beer as is consumed on a typical four-day weekend.

“We’ve never seen anything like it,” Billy DeCain of the Sam Adams Boston Taproom told NBC Boston.

The lemonade stand with an international fan base

In Texas, one family was left with a lifetime of memories after its backyard lemonade stand drew visitors from all over the world.

Heather Hannish and her husband, Ernesto Gloria, sold $2 lemonades and other cold drinks at their backyard stand along the walk to the stadium hosting matches in Arlington, Texas. Hannish and Gloria met fans who traveled from as far as Japan and India, and started keeping a notebook for visitors to leave messages.

“Being able to share this is something that I can’t even begin to articulate or even really fully comprehend,” Hannish told KXAS-TV in Dallas-Fort Worth. “I think really most people are very good at heart and just want the best for everyone else.”

World.title: Hundreds gather for Nolan Wells’ funeral in Mississippi
World.content:
OCEAN SPRINGS, Miss. — Nolan Wells, the Mississippi teenager whose death after a Fourth of July boating trip with friends has spurred national attention, was remembered Monday as a “gentle, calming spirit” during a funeral that attracted hundreds.

Subscribe to read this story ad-free Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

“I want to give all thanks and honor and glory to God for choosing Elmore and me to be Nolan’s parents,” Wells’ mother, Christine Wells-Wonsley, said at the funeral at Center Pointe Church. “We thank you, Lord, for the beautiful 18 years that you blessed us with him.”

Hours before the funeral service in Ocean Springs, Mississippi, which began just after noon local time, people were seen waiting in line, including nearly all of Wells’ high school football teammates. Many of the mourners were seen dressed in black and blue — the colors of Wells’ high school team — per the family’s request.

Ahead of the service, a slideshow of photos of Wells, his friends, and his family was played alongside gospel music. Rev. Al Sharpton delivered the eulogy, and the Wells family’s attorney, Ben Crump, issued a call for justice and asked those with information to come forward.

“Until we get to truth, until we get to justice, we gonna stand up and we gonna keep ringing the justice bells for Nolan Wells,” Crump said, before chanting “Justice for Nolan Wells!”

Christine Wonsley, center, is flanked by her husband Elmore, second from left, attorney Ben Crump, left, and Rev, Al Sharpton during the memorial service. Gerald Herbert / AP

Wells, 18, went missing on July 4 after traveling to Mississippi’s Horn Island for the holiday. His body was found on the shores of Mississippi’s Horn Island days later, spurring an investigation that has yielded few public answers.

“Nolan had such a gentle, calming spirit about him. He had a way of making people feel seen, welcome, and valued,” Wells-Wonsley said. “He could lift your confidence with just a few words, and make you feel like you belonged.”

Wells-Wonsley called her son “protective and nurturing” and spoke about how he once told her he wanted three daughters.

“Your absence has left an emptiness that can never truly be filled,” she said, directly addressing Wells. “In a world that can often feel dark, be like Nolan, be the light that brightens the lives of those around you.”

Elmore Wonsley, Wells’ father, also spoke, noting how proud he was of his son, who he called a model for his younger brothers.

“You grew up to be a very young man that everyone enjoyed to be around,” Wonsley said, also noting his son was often kind to his peers in school.

Football teammates attend the memorial service. Gerald Herbert / AP

In his eulogy, Sharpton also called for unbiased answers and justice related to Wells’ death. He announced that he would offer a $50,000 reward to anyone who provides information leading to an arrest and conviction in Wells’ case.

Tyler Perry, who paid for the funeral, also said he would offer $50,000 for information, Sharpton said at the end of the service. Spike Lee and Terrell Owens also attended the Mississippi funeral.

Following the funeral, Crump spoke to media alongside Wells’ parents, again demanding answers.

Ahead of the service, others who knew Wells spoke about his life and his character.

Wells was “a great young man to coach, and we’re going to miss him dearly for it,” Ocean Springs High School head coach Jake Bramlett told NBC News ahead of Wells’ funeral. “But a little bit of his life that we got to be a part of was outstanding.”

Bramlett described how important it was for the team to show up and support their former teammate, noting that “they’ve done a great job with supporting Nolan’s younger siblings that are on the football team.”

A number of the current players “were brought up under [Wells’] wing,” Bramlett said. “He taught them how to act in the locker room, how to act in the weight room, how to perform on the football field, and that’s just who Nolan was.”

Nolan Wells with his coach, Jake Bramlett. Courtesy Jake Bramlett

Wells’ parents said at a press conference last week that a “party” celebrating Wells will be held at the Jackson County Fairgrounds for friends, family and Wells’ teammates following the funeral service.

“What we’re going to do is kind of have a party to celebrate him,” Wells-Wonsley said of her son Wednesday. “We want to celebrate him, and he would not want us to be sitting around crying and eating.”

The service comes weeks after Wells and a group of friends went to Horn Island, off the coast of Mississippi, to celebrate July 4. The friends returned to the mainland later that afternoon and told police Wells opted to stay behind, saying he would catch a ride back later with others.

Nolan Wells with his parents. Courtesy Wells family

When he didn’t return home that night, his mother reported him missing around midnight. A U.S. park ranger found Wells’ body on the northwest shore of Horn Island on July 6.

It remains unclear how Wells died. Officials have not yet released an autopsy report as the investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death intensified.

Crump and Wells’ parents have said they are leading their own investigation into his death, and performed an independent autopsy on Wells. Crump thanked Colin Kaepernick for paying for the independent autopsy at the news conference Wednesday.

World.title: Judge temporarily halts Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger
World.content:
A U.S. district judge temporarily halted the Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger on Monday, after a coalition of states sued to block the deal.

The temporary restraining order will remain in effect for 14 days, with a hearing set for Aug. 3.

The states' lawsuit "presented compelling evidence that the combined firm resulting from the transaction will possess substantial market share in the wide-release theatrical distribution market," California district judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín wrote in the ruling. "On this combined firm market share alone, the Court is persuaded that it can presume the proposed merger is likely to violate antitrust laws."

"Paramount and Warner Bros. will continue to operate as separate, viable companies competing in the marketplace while they wait for the Court to adjudicate this case," she added.

Attorneys general in 12 states, led by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, sued last week, arguing that the merger would harm competition in the movie industry, result in lower pay for actors and writers and harm consumers by limiting their news and entertainment options.

A Paramount Skydance spokesperson called the states' antitrust arguments "without merit."

"This merger is lawful, pro-competitive, and will benefit consumers, creators, workers, and the entertainment industry," the company said in a statement Monday. "We will continue to vigorously defend the transaction and will look forward to the hearings on the substance of the State AGs' action."

Warner Bros. referred CBS News to Paramount for comment.

Bonta issued a statement calling the judge's ruling "a critical first win in our case to ensure this megamerger never sees the light of day." He said the states are "fighting for a free and fair market and a thriving film and television industry that serves creatives and audiences alike."

New York Attorney General Letitia James, who also joined the lawsuit, said, "Today's decision is an important victory for all those who would be hurt by this merger, and I look forward to continuing to fight this case."

The states' lawsuit alleged that the merger would violate the Clayton Act of 1914, which prevents mergers that may undermine competition or create a monopoly.

Paramount has argued that combining with Warner Bros. will allow it to create more series and films and boost employment opportunities for industry professionals.

The $110 billion merger would unite two of the nation's leading media companies, giving them control of nearly a third of cable programming and more than a third of blockbuster films, according to Bonta's office.

World.title: Spain fans rejoice in World Cup win, but some say Trump photo-bombed team
World.content:
Barcelona — On the streets of Barcelona's historic Gothic Quarter, locals had a lot to celebrate Monday following Spain's 2026 World Cup victory over Argentina. But there were mixed opinions over President Trump lingering on stage around the winning team as cameras snapped shots of the victors hoisting their trophy at the stadium in New Jersey.

"Here in Spain, we have a lot of disagreements in general with the policies and the politics of Trump, but I guess that it's normal that if you are hosting the World Cup that you were there on the stage," Barcelona resident Roger, who declined to give his full name, told CBS News.

"I think it was good for the geopolitics, because I know Trump didn't want Spain to win, and then, bam! In your face!" he said with a smile.

Others, however, failed to see any humor in the president's prolonged presence alongside the Spanish team. After walking on with FIFA boss Gianni Infantino to present Spain's trophy, he then remained on the stage as the players posed for photos. Despite what appeared to be gentle nudging from Infantino, Mr. Trump remained in place just next to the team, smiling and clapping.

Rodri #16 of Spain lifts the trophy while President Trump and FIFA President Gianni Infantino look on during the trophy ceremony on July 19, 2026. Spain beat Argentina, 1-0, in the 2026 World Cup final. Jean Catuffe/Getty

"I think it was kind of disrespectful," one young man, who declined to give his name, told CBS News. "The moment is just for the team, for the players, for the trainers, and he just kind of destroyed it."

"It was quite sad, why would you steal the show or want to show yourself," said another fan, who gave his name as Damiano. "Let the players celebrate on their own. You had the World Cup in your hands, that's enough."

While Mr. Trump's lingering caused some consternation, Spaniards remained on a high Monday following their national triumph. It was, after all, only the second time Spain's team have been crowned FIFA world champs.

Spanish officials said they expect up to a million people to descend on the capital Madrid later Monday to witness the team's open-top bus parade with the trophy.

Rodri of Spain lifts the 2026 World Cup trophy, alongside Spain Football Association president Rafael Louzan, as the Spanish team arrives back in Madrid on July 20, 2026. Pablo Blazquez Dominguez / Getty Images

In the diverse, working class town of Rocafonda, home of Spain's teenage superstar Lamine Yamal, a community watch party for the final match on Sunday was capped by flares and fireworks following the Spaniards' extra time win over Argentina.

The celebrations continued into the night in Barcelona, where a significant number of the Spanish international team play at the club level. Thousands descended onto the city's central Catalunya Plaza and danced and sang into the early hours of Monday morning.

"We are so proud, it's the best feeling in the world," one local said.

World.title: Taylor Farms lettuce sample was false positive for cyclospora, FDA says
World.content:
A sample of lettuce from Taylor Farms that had tested positive for cyclospora was a false positive, the Food and Drug Administration said Sunday. But the FDA said its investigation and data "continue to converge on shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms locations in central Mexico."

In the statement announcing the false positive, the FDA said that as of Sunday it had not found any "confirmed positive sample results for product testing for Cyclospora."

In a subsequent statement Monday, it said, "To clarify, this false-positive lab sample DOES NOT change the basis for FDA's ongoing outbreak investigation or the overwhelming epidemiological data supporting the current voluntary recall by Taylor Farms."

Taylor Farms on Friday said it was "voluntarily removing" iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico after the lettuce had been linked to one of the largest outbreaks of cyclosporiasis in the U.S. in recent years.

"While the FDA traceback is indicating a specific independent farm, which represents less than 1% of the U.S.'s iceberg lettuce supply, as the potential source of the outbreak, we have removed all iceberg lettuce from the region indefinitely," the company said Friday in a statement.

Taylor Farms said Sunday in a statement after the false positive was announced that, "Our thoughts remain with everyone who has fallen ill in this outbreak. We are committed to working with public health authorities as the ongoing outbreak investigation continues."

On Thursday, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention identified lettuce supplied to select Taco Bell restaurants as a source of the multistate outbreak, more than a month after cases first began to appear.

The iceberg lettuce was distributed to Taco Bell restaurants in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia, according to the CDC. Taco Bell said on Friday it had "completed removal of affected Taylor Farms lettuce from our restaurants."

Walmart also announced over the weekend it had removed four Marketside bagged iceberg lettuce salad products from its stores in more than two dozen states, but added there was "no indication that products sold in our stores are affected by the current Cyclospora investigations."

The outbreak, first reported in May, has spread to 34 states and sickened more than 1,600 people, according to the CDC. However, the CDC's tally lags behind state health departments, which have reported much larger numbers of cases. For instance, the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reported more than 5,000 confirmed cases as of Friday.

No deaths have been reported.

Cyclosporiasis is a food- and waterborne illness caused by the cyclospora parasite, which causes long-lasting, watery and sometimes explosive diarrhea, according to public health experts.

Outbreaks typically occur in late spring and summer and have historically been linked to bagged salads, cilantro, basil, raspberries, snow peas and green onions.

World.title: Watch Live: FBI gives update on fireworks explosion outside NYC federal building
World.content:
An incendiary device went off outside a federal building in Lower Manhattan Monday morning, and a suspect has been taken into custody, the FBI said. The FBI New York Joint Terrorism Task Force is investigating the incident.

The incident happened at 8:20 a.m. outside 26 Federal Plaza, a building that houses dozens of agencies including the FBI, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

The sound of an explosion had authorities running to the steps leading into the building. They found a man with an airsoft rifle, carbon dioxide cartridges, halogen lighting and a helmet, multiple law enforcement sources said.

A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said the man launched fireworks outside the building, poured gasoline on the stairs and set it on fire. The fire department responded to put out flames, and the man was taken into custody.

Heavy smoke was seen outside 26 Federal Plaza after an explosion caused by fireworks, sources said. CBS News New York

Sources described the suspect as an anti-ICE activist. They said he had a small cart with him with the slogan "ICE off our streets" written on it.

A Federal Protective Service officer "swiftly tackled and detained the agitator, sustaining minor injuries during the incident," DHS said in a statement.

"At this time, our Joint Terrorism Task Force is investigating this as an anti-government attack on a federal facility," said FBI official James Barnacle.

BB or airsoft guns, commercial-grade fireworks found

The suspect was carrying two types of guns that appeared to be realistic-looking BB guns or airsoft guns, according to preliminary information. One of the two was some type of long gun carried in a grocery cart, law enforcement sources told CBS News.

CBS News law enforcement analyst Richard Esposito described the materials as "things you might use in paintball-type events."

The DHS spokesperson said the man's bag contained two pellet guns and a manifesto.

The sources said an initial review found no shots were fired.

An airsoft rifle, carbon dioxide cartridges, halogen lighting and a helmet were among the items found at 26 Federal Plaza after an explosion. CBS News New York

4 minor injuries at 26 Federal Plaza, firefighters say

Firefighters said four people had minor, non-life-threatening injuries, and one was transported to a local hospital.

One person was grazed by the fireworks, a DHS spokesperson said. A security officer also had minor injuries after tackling the suspect.

Video from the scene showed heavy smoke in front of the building and law enforcement arresting a man.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the incident "deeply disturbing."

"My team is in touch with the NYPD, and we will support the federal investigation. Our administration will continue to ensure that every New Yorker is safe in their city — and hold accountable any who threaten that," he wrote, in part, on social media.

Police said people should expect traffic delays, mass transit disruptions and road closures near Worth Street and Lafayette Street. They are urging people to avoid the area.

World.title: Darline Graham, Lindsey Graham's sister, says she'll run for full Senate term
World.content:
Washington — Sen. Darline Graham, who is serving out the remainder of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's term in the Senate, said Monday that she will seek a full term for the South Carolina seat her brother held for more than two decades.

"I've made a decision," Graham told Fox News. "I'm in."

The late senator, who died on July 11, had secured the GOP nomination in June for what would have been his fifth term representing South Carolina. With his death, the Republican candidate in the South Carolina Senate race will be determined by a special primary election. Republicans seeking the Senate seat may file between July 21 and July 28, before an Aug. 11 primary to decide who will take on Democrat Annie Andrews in November.

Graham, 62, was sworn in last week, after South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to serve out the remainder of her brother's term, which runs through early January. Graham, who doesn't have a background in elected office, had a career in disabilities services and most recently served as commissioner of the South Carolina Commission for the Blind. She said upon accepting the appointment that finishing her brother's term "is what Lindsey would have wanted," noting that she planned to "honor him in this way."

President Trump publicly encouraged Graham to run for a six-year term, writing in a post on Truth Social after meeting with her at the White House last week that she would have his "Complete and Total Endorsement."

"I hope Darline does this, in that there would be nobody better to honor the legacy of her beloved brother, Lindsey," Mr. Trump said.

In an interview with Fox News' Sean Hannity, Graham said, "I have been praying a lot, talking to my family."

"I know I'm a hard worker. I learned that from Lindsey," she said. "I feel like I can do it. I feel an inner peace about it. Will it be difficult? Yes. Absolutely."

The president's endorsement hasn't stopped other Republicans from announcing their intention to run for the six-year term. Rep. Ralph Norman, who's represented South Carolina in the House since 2017, announced a bid on Saturday. And Rep. Russell Fry, who was elected to the House in 2022, announced his candidacy on Monday.

If no candidate secures a majority of the vote in the special primary election, a runoff will be held on Aug. 25.
